lines.narration: In this town, everybody parties except me.
Every dusk, a gold envelope slides under one door.
They threw one for a stop sign. The town fountain got two.
Your envelope comes, they carry you to the square, chanting.
Nine years. My slot never clicks. The neighbor checks it for me.
I practice the chant anyway. Wave. Bow. Smile.
The paperboy got his at nine. The chant made the streetlights pulse.
Then, one night. No music. No lights. Nothing.
Every window dark. An envelope on every doorstep. Unopened.
Nine years of nothing. Tonight they forget me. I almost smiled.
Then my slot clicked. My name, in green ink.
The whole town outside. Unlit lanterns. The neighbor, crying.
They were never parties. They were rehearsals.
They didn't forget me for nine years.
They were making sure I'd say yes.
